name: eMudhra Ltd
title: eMudhra Ltd - 543533 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 core strong (H1 PAT +27%, margin 16.3%), but TLS certificate incident cuts FY27 guidance: revenue ~INR 800 cr from ~825 cr, PAT ~INR 125 cr from ~137 cr, with TLS exit.

summary.headline: eMudhra Q2 FY27 total income rose 19.6% to INR 209 crore and PAT rose 26.3% to INR 33.4 crore, but FY27 guidance was cut after a TLS certificate incident.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed strong core growth: total income INR 209 crore (+19.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 51.3 crore at 24.5% margin, and PAT INR 33.4 crore (+26.3%). H1 total income was INR 402 crore (+23.4%) and PAT INR 65.4 crore (+27%). In October, weak keys were found in eight intermediate certificates in the publicly trusted TLS hierarchy; management revoked them, exited public TLS issuance, and cut FY27 revenue guidance from about INR 825 crore to about INR 800 crore and PAT from about INR 137 crore to about INR 125 crore. Operating cash flow was weighed by lower creditors after timely payments.

segments.name: Enterprise solutions (own five-product platform)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% and now makes up about two-thirds of revenue, per the Chairman. Management said the core grew 23% in H1.

segments.name: Digital trust services (DSC, eSign)
segments.commentary: Conventional digital signatures expected flat to 8-10% growth; token revenue hit by FIPS 140-3 requirement until September. eSign is growing, now 7-8 lakh transactions per day versus 1-2 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Publicly trusted TLS
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; management decided to exit public TLS certificate sales. US TLS business was about INR 4 crore out of about INR 8 crore total TLS business.

segments.name: CRYPTAS (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue run-rate about INR 30 crore in the quarter; management expects about $1 million EBITDA for the year, through December.

segments.name: India vs international
segments.commentary: Total business about INR 800 crore: about INR 275 crore India and about INR 520-525 crore international. International is about two-thirds of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total income cut by about INR 20-23 crore to about INR 800 crore (from about INR 825 crore), per the call.
FY27 PAT cut by about INR 10-12 crore to about INR 125 crore (from about INR 137 crore, about 25% growth originally); impact mainly in H2.
Management expects the incident impact to last about two quarters, then return to business as usual.
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 25% going forward, with focus on higher-margin solutions business.
Incremental FY27 capex about INR 23 crore, mainly completing the data privacy (DPDP) stack, emSigner AI capabilities and ID verification for Google digital signature operations.
Investor meet planned at Trident Hotel, Mumbai, on December 2.
capex_capacity: Incremental planned capex for FY27 about INR 23 crore, directed to completing the DPDP data privacy stack, emSigner AI features and ID verification for digital signature operations.
Management did not disclose capacity or utilisation figures.
eSign volume is about 7-8 lakh per day, up from 1-2 lakh a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Customers face fixed deadlines for post-quantum migration (PQC adoption around 2029), machine and AI agent identity, and data privacy (DPDP); management says these are now board-level topics in banking.
First DPDP deal won in Q2 from an NBFC; DPDP deal sizes INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1 crore for mid-sized entities, INR 2 crore for larger ones.
Post-quantum: several POCs ongoing, one has converted into an order.

Wins: national PKI for Nigeria's certifying authority regulator; first Kazakhstan win with a defence entity; new clients in Indonesia, Philippines, Germany, Qatar and Abu Dhabi; three large enterprise clients in Europe via cross-selling with CRYPTAS.
Trust services pipeline in the UAE is building while the company awaits its trust services licence.
Management says the TLS line faces structural decline: 90-day certificates, free Google DV certificates, ACME auto-renewal, and lower EV demand.

qa_highlights.question: How large is US private PKI as a share of the enterprise business, and what is the 3-5 year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: US TLS was about INR 4 crore of the INR 8 crore TLS total; the US solutions business was about $6-9 million. Management sees private PKI for IoT and devices as a large opportunity, with a healthy pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DPDP opportunity materialising, and what are deal sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: One NBFC deal won in Q2 with more momentum in Q3. Deal sizes INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1 crore for mid-sized entities, INR 2 crore for larger ones.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Trust services trajectory for FY27, and what about CRYPTAS?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional digital signatures are expected flat to 8-10%; eSign is growing. CRYPTAS revenue run-rate about INR 30 crore in the quarter, with about $1 million EBITDA expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Are there existing-client pushbacks or RBI contract ramp-up delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no effect on existing contracts and no terminations. The only affected party was one US university federation, which is continuing with CertiNext and has asked for subcontracted TLS. Some new TLS deals were withdrawn and other deals are slightly delayed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact on CertiNext and the broader enterprise business?
qa_highlights.answer: CertiNext is independent of TLS and is sold standalone in most cases. Management says the impact is limited to the US and a little of the Middle East; Europe, Africa and Far East are largely unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin profile hold beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin is expected at around 25%, driven by the solutions mix.

risks_watch: Reputational spillover from the TLS incident beyond the US TLS customer, especially in the US and Middle East; management expects it to wane over about two quarters.
External review by KPMG and the full ceremony-procedure review are underway; findings are to be shared.
Operating cash flow weakness in H1 from lower creditors after timely payments; receivable days flat.
Trust services (DSC) growth limited to flat to 8-10% with no new government use cases; token margins are lower.
UAE trust services licence still pending.
PQC and DPDP timelines drive the next-year pipeline; conversion of these deals is not yet proven at scale.
Management said the audit and review outcome will be shared; watch for it at the December 2 investor meet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core business and the long-term direction, but candid about the incident and guidance cut. Management was more defensive on the sizing of the impact, and several answers on reputation and TLS economics were repetitive and firm rather than data-led.
key_quotes: We expect the incident to reduce our FY27 total income by about INR 20 crores to INR 23 crores and our PAT by about INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores, largely in the second half.
This affected only our publicly trusted TLS business, which was about 1% of our revenue.
Our digital signatures, e sign, and all five enterprise platforms are not affected.
In our opinion, the impact of the incident may only last for next two quarters, after which it will be business as usual.

adds.what: Incremental capex ~INR 23 crore for DPDP data privacy stack, emSigner AI features and ID verification (software/platform build, not productive capacity count)

growth.why: FY27 total income guidance cut to about INR 800 crore from about INR 825 crore (about 14% growth vs FY26 implied by ~INR 700 crore base, roughly, though base not stated in brief) and PAT to about INR 125 crore from about INR 137 crore after the TLS incident; growth backed by enterprise platform (+36%), eSign volume (7-8 lakh/day vs 1-2 lakh) and first DPDP/PQC wins, but no capacity or order-book n

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided to hold around 25% (Q2 at 24.5%, H1 at 25.3%) with mix shifting to the higher-margin solutions business, but no expansion is guided and TLS and token margins are lower.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management did not disclose capacity or utilisation figures; the only build is about INR 23 crore of software and platform capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: eSign is at 7-8 lakh transactions a day versus 1-2 lakh a year ago and enterprise grew 36%, but the FY27 total income guide was cut to about INR 800 crore from about INR 825 crore, with the impact mainly in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only about INR 23 crore of incremental FY27 capex is planned for DPDP, emSigner AI and ID verification, and no capacity utilisation was disclosed, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 total income guide was cut by about INR 20-23 crore to about INR 800 crore and PAT by about INR 10-12 crore to about INR 125 crore after the TLS incident.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects the incident impact to last about two quarters, and H2 carries most of the PAT cut, while KPMG review findings are still pending and some TLS deals were withdrawn.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DPDP stack, emSigner AI features and ID verification for Google digital signature operations are being completed in FY27, and the first DPDP deal was won in Q2 at INR 40-50 lakh to INR 1 crore.

rows.label: UAE trust services licence
rows.why: Trust services pipeline in the UAE is building, but the licence is still pending, so revenue timing depends on approval.

rows.label: Post-quantum and DPDP conversion
rows.why: One PQC POC has converted to an order and one DPDP deal was won in Q2 from an NBFC, with more momentum expected in Q3, but conversion at scale is not yet proven.

rows.label: KPMG external review outcome
rows.why: Management said the KPMG review and ceremony-procedure review findings will be shared, which could either reassure or add further downside to the TLS and guidance view.

tone.note: Management was confident on the core enterprise business (+36%), eSign growth and the solutions mix, but defensive on sizing the TLS incident impact and repetitive on reputation and TLS economics; analysts pressed on US PKI exposure, DPDP deal momentum and existing-client pushback.
